Your site today

Before choosing anything, a look at ecbernstein.com as it is now, graded in eight areas, then what we keep and what we would change.

EED BERNSTEIN | BIO+–□✕ecbernstein.com/bio/Forty years, Indiana, VeniceAll capitals, one long block

A−Grade

About you

What works

  • A strong record: forty years as an artist, Head of Printmaking at Indiana University, the Venice program and Chiaroscuro Press.
  • A thoughtful artist’s statement on its own page.

What we would change

  • The bio is one long block, set entirely in capitals, so it is hard to read.
  • Nothing about you on the home page; visitors have to find these pages.
EED BERNSTEIN | prints, drawings, & mixed media+–□✕ecbernstein.comOne strong work, full widthSmall, pale menuNothing below the picture

B+Grade

Look and feel

What works

  • It opens on one strong work, Ghost Ship, full width.
  • A quiet white page that never competes with the art.

What we would change

  • The menu is small, pale grey capitals that are hard to read.
  • One picture and nothing below it: no way into the work except the menu.
EED BERNSTEIN | ARTWORK+–□✕ecbernstein.com/artwork/Browse by themeSquares crop each print

BGrade

Showing the work

What works

  • About 55 works in one place, shown large and evenly.
  • Theme filters (anti-war, refugee and immigrant, environment and more) let people browse by subject.

What we would change

  • The squares crop each work, so nobody sees a whole print until they click.
  • No series pages to explain how the works belong together.
EED BERNSTEIN | Tear in the Sky+–□✕ecbernstein.com/portfolio_page/tear-in-the-sky/Medium, size and yearNo price or availabilityOnly a back arrow

B−Grade

Details on each work

What works

  • Every work lists its medium, size and year.
  • A zoom view lets people look closely.

What we would change

  • No price, and no sign of whether it is available.
  • Only a back arrow, with no next or previous work.

CGrade

On a phone

What works

  • The menu folds into one button, and text fits the screen without sideways scrolling.

What we would change

  • The home picture took over four seconds to appear in our test, then filled only the top third of the screen.
  • Pinch-to-zoom is switched off across the site, so nobody can zoom into a print.
EED BERNSTEIN | Tear in the Sky+–□✕ecbernstein.com/portfolio_page/tear-in-the-sky/A clear page titleNo description for Google

C−Grade

Google and sharing

What works

  • Every page has a clear title, like “ED BERNSTEIN | Tear in the Sky”.
  • A site map for Google and a secure address (https).

What we would change

  • 55 of 60 pictures have no description, so Google cannot tell what they show.
  • No page has a Google summary, and links shared in a text or post show no preview.
EED BERNSTEIN | CONTACT+–□✕ecbernstein.com/contact/The only way to buyA plain, easy form

D+Grade

Selling and inquiries

What works

  • A plain form that is easy to fill in.

What we would change

  • It is the only way to buy: “To purchase prints, use the form below”.
  • No way to ask about a work from its own page; buyers type the title and hope it matches.

Questions

Tap a question to see the answer.

The price

What do I get for the price?

A finished website, live on your own address. We design every page in the look you choose, move all 55 works over with your details, build the features of your size, make your rounds of changes, and test it on phones and computers before it goes live.

Why are some looks only at the bigger sizes?

Those looks are built from pages and pieces that only the bigger sizes include, such as series pages, a print shop and more movement.

Can I start small and move up later?

Yes. Moving up a size costs only the difference, at any time: $1,000 from $999 to $1,999, or $3,000 from $1,999 to $4,999.

How do I pay?

Half when we start and half when the site goes live, by bank transfer, Zelle or Venmo.

How long does it take?

About 2 to 4 weeks, depending on the size. You hear from us every week, and again each time a round of changes is ready to look at.

What is a round of changes?

Every design gets our full effort from the first draft. A round of changes is your turn to look at the finished pages and ask for anything different: another order, other wording, a color adjusted, details polished. We make them and show you again. Portfolio includes 1 round, Gallery 2 and Collection 3.

Can I see it before it goes live?

Yes. Each round comes with a private link you can open on your phone or computer, and nothing goes live until you say so.

What if none of the looks feels right?

At $1,999 and $4,999 you can create your own look from the parts you like. Within any look, your rounds of changes cover what you want adjusted.

After launch

Do I need a monthly plan?

No. The site keeps running without one, and the only running cost is your web address, about $15–20 a year, which is in your name and paid by you directly. We set it up. Any change you want is quoted before we start.

Who makes changes once it is live?

We do. Email what you want changed. On a plan, it comes out of your monthly hours, and we reply within 2 business days on Care, 1 on Studio or the same day on Gallery. New features can be added at their listed price, and anything else is quoted before we start.

Is there a limit on how many works I can add?

No. We add all of your current works when we build the site, with photos and details, so it launches complete. After launch, add as many as you make: any monthly plan covers adding them, and without a plan they are quoted.

What if something breaks?

We fix it for free, whenever it happens.

Can I stop a plan?

Yes, any time, with no minimum. The site stays yours and keeps running.

Who owns the website?

You do, once it is paid for: the design, the code, the pictures and the list of works.

Your work and sales

How do people buy my work?

At every size, each work has a short form that sends the question straight to your email. At $4,999, people can also buy prints and editions by card on the site, paid into your own account. Originals always stay on request.

Can I keep prices private?

Yes, work by work: show the price, show “price on request”, or leave it off.

Do you take a share of sales?

No. Nothing from any sale.

What happens to my current website?

When the new site goes live, your web address moves over to it and links to your old pages forward to the matching new ones.

Will people find me on Google?

Every size is set up so search engines can read it properly, with page titles, descriptions and a map of the site. Nobody can promise a ranking.

Who takes the photos of my work?

We use the photos you already have. We do not provide photography.

Who writes the words?

We write the pages, getting to know you and your work through conversations and your notes. New artwork descriptions come from you. The ones on your current site we bring over, and keep or refine them with you. You approve every word before it goes live.
